report: The renal tissue image shows disorganized, pleomorphic cells with large, hyperchromatic nuclei, suggesting malignant transformation. The absence of normal structures like glomeruli and irregular, densely packed cells indicate renal cell carcinoma. Some areas form gland-like structures, and the scant stroma is infiltrated by these malignant cells. Clear cell features are not observed.

evidence.title: Educational case: basal cell carcinoma and its histologic differential
evidence.text: Basal cell carcinoma shows dermal islands of basophilic tumor cells with peripheral nuclear palisading, stromal retraction, and loose mucinous stroma. Cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma shows invasive islands of pleomorphic keratinocytes arising from the epidermis with prominent nucleoli and increased mitoses. Melanoma can show irregular nests and single pleomorphic pigmented melanocytes within the epidermis and dermis.

evidence.title: Various antibody clones of Napsin A, TTF-1, and p40 in non-small cell lung carcinoma
evidence.text: This tissue-microarray study evaluated CK5, p63, and p40 as squamous markers and Napsin A and TTF-1 as lung adenocarcinoma markers. Reported performance varied by marker and antibody clone, and combining Napsin A with TTF-1 improved sensitivity.

evidence.title: Colorectal carcinoma: pathologic aspects
evidence.text: Colorectal adenocarcinoma commonly forms malignant glands. Invasion can be accompanied by desmoplastic stroma, and glandular lumina frequently contain characteristic dirty necrosis. Benign colonic mucosa retains orderly crypt architecture and mature goblet cells without dysplasia.

evidence.title: Immunostaining for TTF-1, Napsin A, p40, and cytokeratin 5 aids differential diagnosis of NSCLC
evidence.text: The study compared marker combinations for separating lung adenocarcinoma from squamous cell carcinoma. TTF-1 and Napsin A supported adenocarcinoma, while p40 and CK5 supported squamous differentiation; the combined panel was more informative than a single stain.

evidence.title: Histologic features of cytomegalovirus esophagitis
evidence.text: CMV cytopathic effect is typically found in endothelial and stromal cells at the ulcer base. Histology may show cytomegaly, eccentrically positioned basophilic intranuclear inclusions surrounded by a clear halo, pale perinuclear regions, and an owl-eye appearance; CMV immunohistochemistry can confirm infected cells.

This tissue-microarray study evaluated CK5, p63, and p40 as squamous markers and Napsin A and TTF-1 as lung adenocarcinoma markers. Reported performance varied by marker and antibody clone, and combining Napsin A with TTF-1 improved sensitivity.

Colorectal adenocarcinoma commonly forms malignant glands. Invasion can be accompanied by desmoplastic stroma, and glandular lumina frequently contain characteristic dirty necrosis. Benign colonic mucosa retains orderly crypt architecture and mature goblet cells without dysplasia.

CMV cytopathic effect is typically found in endothelial and stromal cells at the ulcer base. Histology may show cytomegaly, eccentrically positioned basophilic intranuclear inclusions surrounded by a clear halo, pale perinuclear regions, and an owl-eye appearance; CMV immunohistochemistry can confirm infected cells.

review.assessment: The report describes a malignant renal tumor with glandular features but explicitly notes the absence of clear cell characteristics, contradicting the vision-model predictions of clear cell carcinoma.
rationale: The de-identified report identifies the tissue as renal and suggests renal cell carcinoma, but explicitly states 'Clear cell features are not observed'.
CONCH and PLIP predicted 'kidney renal clear cell carcinoma', which is directly contradicted by the report's observation of absent clear cell features.
Other model outputs (MUSK, QUILTNET) predicted non-renal sites (breast, lung, glioma) which conflict with the report's identification of renal tissue.
discrepancies: Vision models CONCH and PLIP suggest clear cell carcinoma, while the report explicitly denies clear cell features.
MUSK and QUILTNET outputs are inconsistent with the renal origin stated in the report.
recommended_review: Pathologist review to determine the specific renal cell carcinoma subtype (e.g., papillary or chromophobe) given the absence of clear cell features and presence of gland-like structures.
limitations: Retrieved literature provided general morphology for lung and colorectal cancers but contained no specific data on renal cell carcinoma subtypes to aid differential diagnosis.
